page: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

This server includes 472 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable. In benchmark evaluations, the D8lds_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring 2166.0 on Geekbench single-core and achieving 31.52 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8360.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 7990.55. Memory bandwidth is measured at 621.35 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 67.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

Due to its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, this instance is not designed for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data caching. However, the high CPU clock speed and AMX instruction support make it highly efficient for compute-bound tasks, lightweight machine learning inference, and text processing. It achieves a strong text generation speed of 313.4 tokens/sec on small 135M LLM models, though performance drops significantly to 7.97 tokens/sec on medium 7B models. This profile is well-suited for web serving, software compilation, and lightweight batch processing where compute power is prioritized over RAM capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v6 is an x86_64 compute-focused virtual machine powered by an 8-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 4 physical cores, 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), and 472 GB of local storage. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2166.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.52 GB/sec, alongside moderate multi-core capabilities. With its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D8lds_v6 is optimized for compute-bound workloads rather than memory-heavy applications. It is highly suited for static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference on smaller models.
